title: Smoked Aji Amarillo Potato Dumplings
summary: This remarkable dish brings a bold contemporary twist to classic Andean cuisine by focusing on deep smoked flavors and delicate potato dough. Featuring smoked aji amarillo blended directly into yellow potato pastry, these handcrafted dumplings deliver an impressive depth of warmth without overpowering the palate. The interior showcases a savory filling of slow-cooked onions, ground beef, black olives, and hard-boiled egg pieces, echoing the traditional empanada tradition in a tender steamed form. Designed for special gatherings, this recipe balances rich earthiness with bright chili notes. A light drizzle of lime-infused oil and fresh cilantro leaves provides a vibrant finishing touch that cuts through the hearty dumpling texture. Serve these dumplings immediately after steaming alongside a cool rocoto dipping sauce to elevate your dinner experience. Every component can be prepped ahead of time, making this item an ideal focal point for structured multi-course meals. Enjoy the synthesis of ancient Peruvian tubers with modern smoking techniques in this truly unique culinary creation that will delight all guests.

steps.step: Place the washed yellow potatoes into a pot of salted water and bring to a boiling point.
Cook the potatoes until completely soft when tested with a thin metal tester probe.
Drain the hot water thoroughly and let the steam dissipate from potatoes for five minutes.
Peel the warm skins carefully using a small paring knife and discard all peeled skins.
Pass the peeled hot potatoes through a fine potato ricer into a spacious glass bowl.
Add the smoked aji amarillo paste to the riced potatoes while still moderately warm.
Sprinkle the fine sea salt and cassava starch evenly over the potato dough mixture.
Knead the mixture gently by hand until a smooth uniform yellow dough forms completely.
Add one tablespoon of vegetable oil and knead for another full minute to combine.
Cover the bowl with a damp cloth and let the potato dough rest at room temperature.
Divide the rested potato dough into twelve equal portions on a lightly dusted surface.
Roll each portion of dough into a round ball using the palms of your clean hands.
Flatten each dough ball into a flat round disc roughly three inches in diameter.
Cover the prepared discs with plastic wrap so they remain moist prior to filling.
Heat the annatto oil in a heavy frying pan set over medium flame for two minutes.
Add the finely diced red onion and cook until translucent and soft for five minutes.
Stir in the minced garlic and fry for one minute until fragrant and lightly golden.
Add ground beef to the skillet and break it apart into small crumbs with a spoon.
Season the beef mixture with ground cumin dried oregano black pepper and fine salt.
Cook the meat mixture until fully browned and all juices have evaporated completely.
Add chopped black olives and sweet raisins to the skillet and stir well to mix.
Pour in a small splash of water to lift any caramelized bits from pan bottom.
Remove the pan from heat and allow the cooked beef mixture to cool down completely.
Chop the hard boiled eggs into small even cubes on a clean cutting board surface.
Fold the chopped hard boiled eggs and cilantro gently into the cooled beef mix.
Taste the filling and adjust salt or pepper levels if required for balanced flavor.
Divide the beef filling into twelve equal portions using a small ice cream scoop.
Place the filling bowl near your prep area for rapid assembly of potato dumplings.
Place one dough disc onto the palm of your hand and create a gentle cup shape.
Spoon one portion of beef filling into the center of the shaped potato dough disc.
Fold the edges of dough over filling and pinch tightly together to seal complete.
Smooth the exterior seam gently using lightly oiled fingers to prevent cracking.
Repeat the filling process for all remaining dough discs until twelve dumplings form.
Line a bamboo steamer basket with parchment paper punctured with small steam holes.
Arrange the assembled dumplings inside steamer basket leaving space between each.
Set the steamer over a pot of boiling water and cover securely with bamboo lid.
Steam dumplings over medium high steam for exactly twelve minutes until firm.
Whisk rocoto paste evaporated milk lime juice and olive oil for dipping sauce.
Season dipping sauce with a pinch of sugar white vinegar and salt to taste well.
Carefully remove steamer lid allowing hot steam to vent away from your face.
Transfer hot dumplings gently onto serving plates using a wide slotted spatula.
Garnish with fresh parsley leaves and serve immediately alongside rocoto sauce.
